blocks.text: 1.1. Product Introduction
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Celltrion (also referred to as "Applicant" in this review) has submitted a biologics license application (BLA) under section 351(k) of the Public Health Service Act (PHS Act) for CT-P43 (non-proprietary name: ustekinumab-stba; proprietary name: STEQEYMA) as a proposed interchangeable biosimilar to US-licensed Stelara (US-Stelara, ustekinumab). CT-P43 is a recombinant human immunoglobulin isotype class G subclass 1 kappa monoclonal antibody (mAb) that belongs to the pharmacologic class of Interleukin -23 (IL-23) and Interleukin-12 (IL-12) antagonists.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Applicant is seeking licensure for CT-P43 injection as follows:
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: CT-P43, 45 mg/0.5 mL prefilled syringe (PFS) for subcutaneous use as interchangeable with US-Stelara injection 45 mg/0.5 mL PFS for subcutaneous use.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: CT-P43, 90 mg/mL PFS for subcutaneous use as interchangeable with US-Stelara injection 90 mg/mL PFS for subcutaneous use.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: CT-P43, 130 mg/26 mL single-dose vial for intravenous (IV) use as interchangeable with US-Stelara injection 130 mg/26 mL single-dose vial for IV use.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Agency agreed to the Applicant's deferral plan for the development of a 45 mg/0.5 mL single dose vial presentation for subcutaneous use for pediatric patients weighing less than 60 kg. The proposed strengths, dosage form, and routes of administration of CT-P43 are the same as those approved for US-Stelara.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Celltrion is seeking licensure of CT-P43 for the following indications for which USlicensed Stelara is approved:
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (Ps) in adult patients and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older, who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Active psoriatic arthritis in adult patients and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Moderately to severely active Crohn's disease in adults
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in adults
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Although the Division of Dermatology and Dentistry (DDD) is the lead division for this application and provided the written clinical review, clinical input pertaining to their respective indications was obtained from the Division of Gastroenterology (DG) and the Division of Rheumatology and Transplant Medicine (DRTM) during the course of the review.

blocks.text: 1.3. Mechanism of Action, Route of Administration, Dosage Form, Strength, and Conditions of Use Assessment
section_path: 1.3. Mechanism of Action, Route of Administration, Dosage Form, Strength, and Conditions of Use Assessment
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: CT-P43 is a recombinant human immunoglobulin isotype class G subclass 1 kappa (IgGk1) monoclonal antibody (mAb) that binds to the shared p40 subunit of interleukin12 (IL-12) and interleukin-23 (IL-23) to block the IL-12- and IL-23-mediated signaling. Interleukin-23 and IL-12 are naturally occurring cytokines that are involved in inflammatory and immune responses in inflammatory conditions such as plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis (among others). Interleukin-12 stimulates natural killer cells and drives the differentiation of CD4+ T cells toward the T helper 1 phenotype, while IL-23 induces and maintains the IL-17 pathway. CT-P43 has the same mechanisms of action as that of US-licensed Stelara to the extent known.

blocks.text: 1.7. Conclusions on Approvability
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In considering the totality of the evidence submitted, the data submitted by the Applicant demonstrate that CT-P43 is highly similar to US-licensed Stelara, notwithstanding minor differences in clinically inactive components, and that there are no clinically meaningful differences between CT-P43 and US-licensed Stelara in terms of the safety, purity, and potency of the product. The data and information provided by the Applicant are sufficient to demonstrate that CT-P43 can be expected to produce the same clinical result as USlicensed Stelara in any given patient and that the risk in terms of safety or diminished efficacy of alternating or switching between use of CT-P43 and US-licensed Stelara is not greater than the risk of using US-licensed Stelara without such alternation or switch. The information submitted by the Applicant, including adequate justification for extrapolation of data and information, demonstrates that CT-P43 may be approved for each of the following indications for which US-licensed Stelara has been previously approved and for which the Applicant is seeking licensure of CT-P43:

section_path: 3. Summary of Conclusions of Other Review Disciplines
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: OPQ is not recommending approval of BLA 761338 for CT-P43 manufactured by Celltrion, Inc. The data submitted in this application are not sufficient to support the conclusion that the manufacture of CT-P43 is well-controlled and leads to a product that is pure, safe, and potent. Multiple product quality deficiencies including inadequate control of drug product and insufficient data to support sterility assurance of the CT-P43 130 mg/26 mL (5 mg/mL) single-dose vial drug product have been identified and listed in the OPQ executive summary. From an OPQ perspective, this BLA is not recommended for approval in its present form until the product quality deficiencies are satisfactorily resolved.

4.1. Nonclinical E I Executive Summary and Recommendation
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The FDA has determined that animal testing is unnecessary to support a demonstration of biosimilarity between CT-P43 and US-Stelara. Refer to the OPQ section for detailed documentation (Section 3.1). From a nonclinical perspective, because the toxicity of ustekinumab products, barring differences in clinical pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters, is a direct function of their affinity to bind to the shared p40 subunit of interleukin-12 (IL12) and interleukin-23 (IL-23) to block the IL-12- and IL-23-mediated signaling, the comprehensive battery of in vitro cell-free and cell-based studies are considered more sensitive than animal studies in detecting differences, between CT-P43 and US-Stelara. In the absence of specific pharmacokinetic, physicochemical, or other identifiable concerns, in vivo animal studies are not anticipated to provide additional meaningful information to inform the evaluation of toxicity. Animal studies with CT-P43 are not required to support this 351(k) application.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The clinical pharmacology review for this BLA primarily focused on the PK similarity study (Study CT-P43 1.2) and additional PK and immunogenicity data from the comparative clinical study (Study CT-P43 3.1) as these studies provided primary supportive evidence for demonstration of the biosimilarity of CT-P43. A summary of study outcome from the first PK similarity study, Study CT-P43 1.1 will be provided in this review for completeness; however, this failed PK similarity study would have limited regulatory utility. Study CT-P43 1.1 was designed as a two part randomized, doubleblind, three-arm, parallel-group, single-dose, active comparator, first-in-human study in healthy male subjects conducted in Canada. In part 2 of the Study CT-P43 1.1, PK similarity of the proposed biosimilar, CT-P43 was assessed compared to EU-Stelara and US-Stelara in a three-way parallel treatment design, where, the upper limits of the 90% confidence intervals (CIs) exceeded 125.00% for the AUC0-inf comparison of CTP43 to EU-Stelara and to US-Stelara. The applicant conducted a root cause analysis with the aim to identify reasons for the failure to demonstrate PK similarity in Study CTP43 1.1 Part 2. During investigation of Study CT-P43 1.1 Part 2, it was found that the clinical batches of CT-P43 used in the study had a higher protein content compared to EU-Stelara and US-Stelara batches. The post-hoc statistical analysis was conducted after dose correction in order to adjust for protein content of clinical batches and it was observed that the upper bounds of the 90% CIs for AUC0-inf were closer to 125% which supported that the protein content difference impacted the PK comparisons between CT-P43 and Stelara products. Subsequently, Study CT-P43 1.2 was conducted with revised inclusion criteria to enroll a more homogenous population, and an increased sample size considering %CV in historical data, and the Applicant used US and EU Stelara batches with a similar protein content compared to the proposed biosimilar, CTP43. Refer to Clinical pharmacology appendix for details on Study CT-P43 1.1. The Applicant provided sufficient details of the study design differences between Study CTP43 1.1 and Study CT-P43 1.2. Based on these justifications, FDA considers Study CTP43 1.2 more appropriately designed to comparatively asses PK between the products.

blocks.text: In the PK similarity study, CT-P43 1.2, the 90% confidence intervals (CIs) for the geometric mean ratios (GMRs) of CT-P43 to US-Stelara, CT-P43 to EU-Stelara, and EU-Stelara to US-Stelara were contained within the prespecified margin of 0.8 to 1.25 for AUC0-inf, Cmax and AUClast (Table 6). The results of the PK similarity study demonstrated that PK similarity was established between CT-P43, US-Stelara and EUStelara. The PK similarity study also established the PK component of scientific bridge which supports the relevance of EU-Stelara in the comparative clinical study.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In the PK similarity study in Japanese healthy subjects, Study CT-P43 1.2, following a single 45 mg SC injection of CT-P43, EU-Stelara, or US-Stelara, the 90% CIs for the GMRs of CT-P43 to EU-Stelara, CT-P43 to US-Stelara, and EU-Stelara to US-Stelara for the tested PK parameters (i.e., AUC0-inf, Cmax and AUClast) were all within the prespecified margin of PK similarity of 80-125%. These pairwise comparisons met the pre-specified criteria for PK similarity between CT-P43, EU-Stelara, and US-Stelara; thus, the PK portion of the scientific bridge was established to support the relevance of the data generated using EU-Stelara as a comparator in the comparative clinical study (Study CT-P43 3.1).

blocks.text: In this PK similarity study, the primary endpoints were the PK parameters: AUCinf and Cmax. blocks.label: text
blocks.text: PK similarity among CT-P43, US-Stelara and EU-Stelara has been demonstrated in a 3arm, parallel PK similarity study in healthy Japanese subjects (Study CT-P43 1.2) in this study. PK samples were collected pre-dose on Day 1, and post-dose at 8 hr and 24 hr and on Days 3, 7, 9, 11, 13, 21, 28, 35, 49, 56, 70, 98 and 112. The point estimates and 90% CIs of the GMRs of PK parameters (AUC0-inf, Cmax and AUClast) were all within the pre-defined criteria of 0.8 to 1.25 (Table 6). The mean serum concentration-time profiles were similar among CT-P43, US-Stelara and EU-Stelara treatment groups (Figure 4).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The PK parameters following a single 45 mg SC dose of CT-P43, US-Stelara and EUStelara are summarized in Table 7. In general, PK parameters and inter-subject variabilities were comparable across the three treatment groups. This study utilized EU Stelara and US Stelara batches with similar protein content compared to CT-P43. The protein content in CT-P43 batch 2NGP01 was 48.60 mg/syringe and the protein content for EU Stelara (batch: LJS3MMH) and US-Stelara drug products [batch: 21E141MF and LJS3MMA) was 49.29 mg/syringe.

section_path: 5.3.6. PK of CT-P43 and EU-Stelara in Subjects with Psoriasis
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Study CT-P43 3.1 is a comparative clinical efficacy and safety study comparing CT-P43 with EU-Stelara in subjects with moderate to severe chronic psoriasis. The study consisted of two treatment periods. In treatment period 1, the enrolled subjects were randomized to receive either 45 or 90 mg of CT-P43 or EU-Stelara by SC injection via PFS at Weeks 0, 4, 16 weeks based on subject's baseline body weight (45 mg for ≤100 kg vs. 90 mg for >100 kg). The primary clinical endpoint was improvement of baseline PASI score. Subjects who achieved at least 50% improvement from baseline in PASI (PASI 50) at Week 12 continue study drug administration in the Treatment Period 2 in all treatment groups. At Week 16, all subjects in the EU-Stelara group were randomly assigned again in a ratio of 1:1 to either continue EU-Stelara or undergo a transition to CT-P43. All subjects who were initially randomized to the CT-P43 group on Day 1 (Week 0) continued their treatment with CT-P43 until Week 40. Overall, the dosing schedule was as below:

The comparable concentrations across treatment groups in the psoriasis subjects in treatment period 2, together with the results of the PK similarity study (Study CT-P43 1.2) supports a demonstration that there is no meaningful difference between CT-P43 and EU-Stelara.

blocks.text: 5.4.1. Design features of the clinical immunogenicity assessment
section_path: 5.4.1. Design features of the clinical immunogenicity assessment
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The main objective for evaluation of the immunogenicity potential of CT-P43 was to address the immune response, by monitoring the formation of anti-drug antibody (ADA), including NAb and relate these to relevant clinical endpoints in clinical studies that have adequate sensitivity to detect an impact on PK, efficacy and safety (e.g., potentially immune-mediated adverse events [AEs]). Immunogenicity was assessed in healthy subjects following a single 45 mg SC dose of CT-P43, US-Stelara or EU-Stelara in Study CT-P43 1.2. Further, immunogenicity in psoriasis subjects was assessed following multiple SC doses of CT-P43 and EU-Stelara in Study CT-P43 3.1. The following section provides a high-level summary of the immungoenicity assessment. See Figure 2 and Figure 3 for more details regarding the study designs.
section_path: 5.4.1. Design features of the clinical immunogenicity assessment
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.4.2. Immunogenicity endpoints
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Blood samples collected for immunogenicity assessment were first tested for ADA. Samples that tested positive for ADA were further tested for Nab.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header

section_path: 5.4.3. Immunogenicity assay's capability of detecting the ADA and NAb in the presence of proposed product, U.S.-licensed reference product, and nonU.S.-licensed comparator product (as applicable) in the study samples
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Applicant developed binding and neutralizing antibody assays that are suitable for detecting ADA and NAb in the presence of expected levels of CT-P43, US-Stelara and EU-Stelara. Refer to the OPQ Immunogenicity assay review for more details.
section_path: 5.4.3. Immunogenicity assay's capability of detecting the ADA and NAb in the presence of proposed product, U.S.-licensed reference product, and nonU.S.-licensed comparator product (as applicable) in the study samples
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The immunogenicity data provided by Celltrion using the validated ADA and NAb assays discussed in the submission, indicate that both sets of assays are suitable for intended purpose as they are able to detect and confirm high rates of ADA and NAb+ samples for clinical studies ( CT-P43 1.2 and CT-P43 3.1). It should be noted that the immunogenicity results from study CT-P43 1.1 were not connsidered for the purpose of biosimilarity.

section_path: In healthy subjects following a single SC dose of 45 mg (Study CT-P43 1.2)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The immunogenicity of CT-P43 was numerically lower compared to those of US-Stelara and EU-Stelara in healthy adult subjects following a single 45 mg SC dose. The incidence of ADA and NAb by treatment group in Study CT-P43 1.2 is summarized in Table 10. The differences were not considered to be clinically significant.

blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In study CT-P43 3.1, the immunogenicity results in both dose groups (45 mg and 90 mg) indicate that CT-P43 appears to be less immunogenic. In the 45 mg dose group, 21 (10.7%) and 42 (21.1%) subjects in the CT-P43 and EU-Stelara groups, respectively, were found to have at least one ADA positive result after exposure to the study drug up to week 16 (Table 11). In 90 mg group, 5 (8.5%) and 19 (35.2%) subjects in the CT-P43 and EU-Stelara groups, respectively, exhibited at least one ADA positive result after exposure to the study drug at end of treatment period I (prior to re-randomization to start switching treatment) (Table 12).
section_path: In healthy subjects following a single SC dose of 45 mg (Study CT-P43 1.2)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer

blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: After week 16 in treatment period II, subjects in EU-Stelara group were re-randomized to EU Stelara maintenance and Switching treatment group where the subject received CT-P43. At the end of treatment period II, in 45 mg dose group, the ADA response rate in EU-Stelara maintenance and Switching arm were 33.7% and 30.9%, respectively (Table 11). In contrast to 45 mg group, a numerical slight increase in ADA response rate was observed in switching arm in 90 mg group. At the end of treatment period II, in 90 mg dose group, the ADA response rate in EU-Stelara maintenance and Switching arm were 37% and 44.4%, respectively (Table 12).

blocks.text: In healthy subjects, in the PK similarity study CTP-P43 1.2, the development of ADAs resulted in decrease in AUCinf in each treatment group. The development of ADAs increased the clearance and decreased the half-lives of each study drug, (CT-P43, USStelara and EU-Stelara). Similarly, in the multiple dose comparative clinical study in subjects with plaque psoriasis, the development of ADAs resulted in a decrease in trough concentrations in both CT-P43 and EU-Stelara at each study visit through Week 28 (Table 15).

blocks.text: Impact of ADA on Safety Overall, no apparent impact of ADA on safety of CT-P43, US-Stelara, or EU-Stelara was observed in the PK similarity study (CT-P43 1.2) and clinical similarity study (CTP43 3.1). Cases of injection site reactions were reported in all three treatment groups. In general, the number of injection site injuries were slightly higher in the CT-P43 treatment group compared to the EU-Stelara and US Stelara treated groups. There were no meaningful differences seen in other immunogenic safety events (i.e. anaphylaxis, cytokine release syndrome) among the 3 treatment arms. Refer to Section 6.4: Clinical conclusion on immunogenicity for information on impact of ADA response on safety.

blocks.text: Comparative Efficacy: The comparative efficacy of CT-P43 and EU-Stelara was evaluated in Study CT-P43 3.1, a double-blind, randomized, multi-center, parallel-group, efficacy and safety study in subjects with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (PsO) during 40 weeks of treatment. Comparative efficacy were assessed for primary endpoint, the mean percent improvement in PASI at Week 12. The 90% confidence interval (CI) for the treatment difference based on the mean percent change from baseline in PASI at Week 12 for the Modified Intent-to-Treat (mITT) Analysis Set, the supportive per- protocol (PP) Analysis Set, as well as sensitivity analyses, all fall within the similarity margins of ±10 [mITT: (-0.23, 4.32), PP: (-0.29, 4.29)]. Thus, the study showed no meaningful differences between the CT-P43 and EU-Stelara treatment arms regarding the primary efficacy endpoint. In addition, secondary efficacy endpoints demonstrated no meaningful differences between the CT-P43 and EU-Stelara treatment arms.

blocks.text: Study CT-P43 3.1 was a randomized, active-controlled, double-blind, multicenter, Phase 3 study designed to evaluate efficacy, PK, QoLand overall safety including immunogenicity of CT-P43 compared with EU-Stelara administered by subcutaneous (SC) injection via pre-filled syringe (PFS) in subjects with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The duration of the study was to be up to 58 weeks, which included Screening (up to 6 weeks), Treatment Period I and II (up to 40 weeks), and off-dose follow-up period (12 weeks) prior to the End-of-Study (EOS) visit.

blocks.text: On Day 1 (Week 0), subjects who met all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria were enrolled in the study and randomly assigned in 1:1 ratio (the first randomization) to receive either CT-P43 or EU-Stelara by SC injection. In particular, they received either CT-P43 or EU-Stelara 45 mg (who weighed ≤100 kg) or 90 mg (who weighed >100 kg) administered subcutaneously at Weeks 0, 4, 16, 28, and 40 based on subject's baseline body weight. Treatment assignment was stratified by the following: country, body weight (≤100 kg vs. >100 kg), prior biological use approved for psoriasis treatment (Yes or No).
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.2. Review of Comparative Clinical Studies with Statistical Endpoints

Subjects who were initially randomly assigned to EU-Stelara were randomized again in a ratio of 1:1 to either continue EU-Stelara or transition to CT-P43. All subjects who were initially randomly assigned to CT-P43 at Day 2 will continue their treatment with CT-P43 until Week 40. The second randomization of the EU-Stelara treatment group was stratified by dose at Week 16 (45 mg vs. 90 mg).

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: For the primary efficacy endpoint, the primary efficacy analysis was conducted on the mITT Set using an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model coupled with multiple imputation (MI) with the missing at random (MAR) assumption for missing data handling. The ANCOVA model included the treatment as a fixed effect and country, baseline body weight, prior biologic use approved for psoriasis treatment, and baseline PASI score as covariates.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Handling of Missing Data
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.2. Review of Comparative Clinical Studies with Statistical Endpoints
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Multiple imputation with the MAR assumption was applied using MI procedure in SAS ® . The multiple imputed datasets were generated based on regression models with country, baseline body weight, prior biologic use approved for psoriasis treatment, baseline PASI score and treatment group as covariates. All subjects with baseline PASI score in mITT Set was included in the analysis. Ten imputed datasets were created and, in the case that the imputed value of percent improvement from baseline in PASI score at Week 12 is over 100, it was replaced with 100. ANCOVA for the mean percent improvement in PASI at Week 12 was applied to each of the imputed datasets. The results from each set of imputed datasets were then be combined using MIANALYZE procedure in SAS ® based on Rubins' rules for final statistical inference.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.2. Review of Comparative Clinical Studies with Statistical Endpoints
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: For the comparison of efficacy, if the 90% CI for the treatment difference in the mean percent improvement in PASI between the CT-P43 and EU-Stelara falls entirely within the specified margins of ± 10%, we conclude that there are no meaningful differences between the two products with respect to efficacy.

section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations

blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: When the applicant generated the multiple imputed datasets, they only included the baseline covariates in the model to impute the missing PASI values at Week 12, rather than including their historical non-missing PASI values in the previous weeks as well in the model. The latter approach will produce more accurate imputation then the former approach. However, considering that there are only 5 subjects in this study with missing data and the study result is robust, use of either imputation approach results in the same conclusion.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: To assess the robustness, a sensitivity analysis using tipping point analysis under missing not at random (MNAR) scenario was conducted for the primary efficacy endpoint in the mITT Set. In the tipping point analysis, imputed values were shifted gradually from the imputed values by MI under MAR by treatment groups (CT-P43 vs. EU-Stelara) to make MNAR scenarios. A point estimate and 90% CI for treatment difference were provided using an ANCOVA considering the treatment as a fixed effect and country, baseline body weight, prior biologic use approved for psoriasis treatment and baseline PASI score as covariates under the scenarios.

blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Two sensitivity analyses with 'best-worst case' scenario and 'worst-best case' scenario were conducted to assess the robustness. First, a 'best-worst case' scenario dataset was generated on the assumption that the missing values in CT-P43 were imputed with '100' percent meaning that PASI scores at Week 12 go down to all zeros, and the missing values in EU-Stelara were imputed with '0' percent meaning that PASI scores at Week 12 remain unchanged from baseline. Then a 'worst-best case' scenario dataset was generated on the premise that the missing values in CT-P43 were imputed with '0' percent and the missing values in EU-Stelara were imputed with '100' percent. Point estimate and 90% CI for treatment difference was also provided using an ANCOVA considering the treatment as a fixed effect and country, baseline body weight, prior biologic use approved for psoriasis treatment and baseline PASI score as covariates under the scenarios.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: PASI score was summarized using descriptive statistics of actual value by treatment group at each scheduled visit. blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Table 24 shows the applicant's primary efficacy analysis results for the primary efficacy endpoint, the mean percent improvement from baseline in PASI score at Week 12. The primary efficacy analysis was conducted on the mITT Set using an ANCOVA model with the treatment as a fixed effect and country, baseline body weight, prior biologic use approved for psoriasis treatment and baseline PASI score as covariates, coupled with MI with the MAR assumption for missing data handling. The point estimate (2.05) and 90% CI for the estimate of treatment difference ([-0.23, 4.32]) were entirely within the predefined similarity margin of -10% to 10%, which demonstrated no clinically significant difference between the CT-P43 and EU-Stelara groups in the primary endpoint for the mITT Set. A supportive analysis was conducted using the PPS and the result is consistent with the primary efficacy analysis result (90% CI: [-0.29, 4.29] for the PPS). The reviewer replicated the applicant's analysis results.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: To assess the robustness of the primary efficacy analysis result based on MI with the MAR assumption for missing data handling, the applicant conducted a sensitivity analysis using tipping point analysis under MNAR scenario for the primary efficacy endpoint in the mITT Set. In the tipping point analysis, imputed values for missing data of 5 subjects in the EU-Stelara treatment group were shifted gradually from the imputed values by MI under MAR by treatment groups (CT- P43 vs. EU-Stelara) to make MNAR scenarios while there were no missing cases in the CT- P43 treatment group. The shift occurred within the range of percent improvement from baseline in PASI score at Week 12 (0 to 100) and all possible scenarios were entirely within the equivalence margin of -10% to 10% (Table 25).

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Efficacy data from Study CT-P43 3.1 were compared to the results from Stelara studies. These studies employed the same dosage regimen as that used in Study CTP43 3.1 and the key eligibility criteria were similar to those of Study CT-P43 3.1. All the studies had key eligibility criteria: Plaque-type psoriasis diagnosed >6 months prior, and Plaque-type psoriasis covering at least 10% of total BSA. The Study CT-P43 3.1 had more restrictive criteria (PASI score of ≥12, sPGA score of ≥3).

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Table 32 shows that the proportions of subjects achieving PASI 50, PASI 75, PASI 90, and PASI 100 responses during Treatment Period I were generally similar between the CT-P43 and EU-Stelara groups in the mlTT Set. At Week 12, 96.5%, 82.8%, 50.4%, and 18.4% of the CT-P43 group and 94.9%, 73.9%, 50.2%, and 19.0% of the EUStelara group had PASI 50, PASI 75, PASI 90, and PASI 100 responses, respectively.

blocks.text: Statistical Reviewer's Comment:
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.2. Review of Comparative Clinical Studies with Statistical Endpoints
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: For PASI75 at Week 12, CT-P43 seems to have a higher proportion of responders (82.8%) than EU-Stelara (73.9%). The reported 95% Cl of the risk difference between CT-P43 and EU-Stelara was [1.78, 16.02] (Table 32). While the 95% CI was used by the applicant for exploratory purpose, considering that 90% Cl is usually used for a biosimilar study, the reviewer calculated the 90% Cl for the risk difference, which is [2.93, 14.87]. Additional analyses of the secondary endpoints in Table 32 are consistent with the primary endpoint and the results support a demonstration that there are no clinically meaningful differences between CT-P43 and U.S.-Stelara.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.2. Review of Comparative Clinical Studies with Statistical Endpoints
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: CDTL Comment: From a clinical perspective, no clinically meaningful differences have been demonstrated in terms of efficacy because the primary endpoint 90% CI was contained within the prespecified margins. The PASI 75 endpoint is supportive. It should be noted that continuous endpoints tend to be more powerful than binary endpoints for the same underlying scale, which can translate into seemingly larger estimated treatment effects that may be random, due to the studies being underpowered for the binary endpoint comparisons.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.2. Review of Comparative Clinical Studies with Statistical Endpoints
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Additionally, the secondary endpoints do not appear to show a pattern suggestive of a meaningful difference in PASI response between the two study arms (Table 32). These descriptive secondary endpoints support a demonstration that there are no clinically meaningful differences between CT-P43 and US-Stelara.

blocks.text: To characterize safety, adverse events, laboratory examination, vital signs, hypersensitivity, and immunogenicity were reviewed. The primary study used to evaluate safety was the comparative clinical study CT-P43 3.1, as it provided controlled and blinded comparisons between EUStelara and CT-P43 in subjects with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis for up to 52 weeks. Safety data from the two pharmacokinetics (PK) similarity studies conducted in healthy volunteers, CT-P43 1.1 and CT-P43 1.2, were also briefly reviewed as supportive of the primary

blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Applicant submitted safety data from three clinical studies in support of the BLA, as listed in Table 3 and summarized below. In all three clinical studies, subjects received 45 mg or 90 mg of either CT-P43, EU-Stelara, or US-Stelara. The primary safety data were derived through the conduct of Study CT-P43 3.1. The remaining two studies, CT-P43 1.1 and CT-P43 1.2, were single-dose PK similarity studies in healthy male volunteers. The former of the two studies was conducted in New Zealand, and the latter exclusively enrolled Japanese male volunteers. As such, limited safety data for the intended population can be obtained from these two studies.

blocks.text: CT-P43 1.1 was a randomized, double-blind, 3-arm, parallel group, single dose study in healthy male volunteers to assess the PK similarity of a 45 mg subcutaneous dose of CT-P43, EU-Stelara, or US-Stelara. For Part 1, 30 subjects were randomized to receive CT-P43 (n=14) or EU-Stelara (n=16) and evaluated up to Day 29. For Part 2, 241 subjects were randomized to receive CT-P43 (n=80), EU-Stelara (n=82) or US-Stelara (n=79) and evaluated up to Day 127. CT-P43 1.1 was meant to serve as a bridging study; however, the study failed to establish the PK similarity, as the upper bounds of the 90% CIs for AUC0-inf were over the 125% acceptance range between CT-P43 and USStelara or CT-P43 and EU-Stelara.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
Clinical Studies Used to Evaluate Safety
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: The second PK similarity study, CT-P43 1.2, which met the criteria for establishing the PK similarity, was a randomized, double-blind, 3-arm, parallel group, single dose study to compare the PK and safety of three formulation of ustekinumab (CT-P43, EU-Stelara and US- Stelara) in healthy Japanese male volunteers. The study randomized 331 subjects to receive a single dose of 45 mg SC injection of CT-P43 (n=114), EU-Stelara (n=110) or US-Stelara(n=107) and evaluated the subjects up to Day 113. Safety data from these two PK studies are included for completeness.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
Clinical Studies Used to Evaluate Safety
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: The primary safety data were derived through the conduct of the clinical study CT-P43 3.1, which was a randomized, double blind, active controlled, parallel group study designed to compare efficacy and safety of CT-P43 and EU-Stelara in adults with moderate to severe psoriasis. This study randomized 509 subjects to receive CT-P43 (n=256) or EU-Stelara (n=253). The subjects received an initial dose of study drug 45 or 90mg administered subcutaneously, followed by another dose 4 weeks later, and then every 12 weeks thereafter up to Week 40. The subjects who weighed ≤100kg received 45 mg (1 injection of 45mg/0.5ml) of study drug by SC injection via PFS, and those who weigh >100kg received 90 mg (2 injections of 45 mg/0.5 ml) of study drug by SC injection via PFS.

section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: For the CT-P43 1.1, CT P-43 1.2, and CT-P43 3.1 studies, at every study visit the subjects were asked a "standard question to elicit any medically related changes in their well-being." They were also asked if they had been "hospitalized, had any accidents, used any new medications, or changed concomitant medication regimens (both prescription and over-the-counter medications)."
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Applicant reported that the Investigators' verbatim terms were converted to preferred terms (PTs), according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) v5.0, and the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA). The Applicant defined treatmentemergent AE (TEAE) as any untoward medical occurrence in a subject after administration of a drug, whether or not it was considered drug-related. The Applicant also defined any occurrence that was new in onset or aggravated in intensity or frequency from the baseline condition and abnormal results of diagnostic procedures including laboratory test abnormalities as AEs, if they resulted in discontinuation from the study, required therapeutic intervention or diagnostic evaluation, or were associated with clinical signs or symptoms judged by the investigator to have a significant clinical impact. Disease progression of psoriasis and PsA was not recorded as an AE or SAE. The final monitoring for adverse event was conducted at the EOS visit, which was 12 weeks after the last administration of the study drug.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: applicant

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Applicant reported that the AEs were monitored from the date the subject signed the Informed Consent Form (ICF) until the end-of-study (EOS) visit. All the AEs were reportedly followed until resolution or improvement to baseline, death, confirmed by the investigator that no further improvement could be expected, no more collection of clinical or safety data, or final database closure.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: applicant

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The intensity of an AE referred to the extent to which an AE affected the subject's daily activities. The intensity of the AE was graded based on the CTCAE v5.0, based on the following general:

section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Grade 2: Moderate: minimal, local, or non-invasive intervention indicated or limiting ageappropriate instrumental activities of daily living
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Grade 3: Severe or medically significant but not immediately life-threatening: hospitalization or prolongation of hospitalization indicated or disabling or limiting selfcare activities of daily living

blocks.text: Adverse events of special interest including opportunistic infections and immune-based adverse effects were summarized using grouped MedDRA codes, in addition to presentation of individual adverse event preferred terms. Immune-based adverse effects included injection-site reactions (ISRs), adverse events that fulfill Sampson Criteria, and adverse events identified as potential hypersensitivity/anaphylactic reactions using a system MedDRA standardized MedDRA query (SMQ) that occur in relation to administration of the study drug.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Safety assessments were also performed based on immunogenicity, hypersensitivity monitoring, body weight, vital sign measurements (including blood pressure, pulse and respiratory rates, and body temperature), interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA), chest X-ray, hepatitis B and C, physical examination findings, clinical laboratory analyses, ECGs, AEs (including serious adverse events [SAEs]), adverse events of special interest (AESIs: infections or serious infections, injection site reactions, hypersensitivity reactions, and malignancies), pregnancy tests, prior and concomitant medications, local site pain using 100 mm VAS, and signs and symptoms of tuberculosis. Human immunodeficiency virus status was tested to determine subject's eligibility.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Clinical Reviewer's Introductory Comment on Data Quality: Based on the ADAE.xpt file, the adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) initially appeared to have been appropriately defined, coded, and categorized by the Applicant during the CT-P43 development program. However, review of select adverse event narratives, case report forms (CRFs), and subject updates received from the Applicant after Information Request revealed several instances, where AEs were inappropriately defined or coded or where AEs were omitted. There were instances, where the subjects received treatment-emergent medications without noting concomitant adverse events that led to such medications or where subject narratives noted no therapeutic measures for the AEs, when it is noted elsewhere that specific medications for the AEs had been administered. Below some of the examples are discussed:

blocks.text: Subject (b)(6) was a 62-year-old white female in the CT-P43 maintenance group. Her medical history included hypertension, hyperthyroidism, myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, cholelithiasis, hypercholesterolaemia, obesity, osteoarthritis, plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, asthma, latent tuberculosis, and psoriatic arthropathy. She experienced during TP1 a Grade 2 TEAE of chest pain PT (pain in the precordial area), for which she received treatment-emergent medications in the form of clopidogrel bisulfate and intravenous administration of paracetamol. Per the AE narrative provided by the Applicant, "(i)t is not known from the case report form if therapeutic measures were administered to treat the event," even though the subject's CRF (page 3010, CTD 5.3.5.1, Section 16.3.1) notes that the subject received medication for this AE.

blocks.text: Throughout the study, the subject also had 3 episodes of Grade 3 TEAEs of headache PT (headache syndrome). The investigator deemed the TEAEs to be related to the study drug, and 2 of the 3 episodes resolved after intramuscular metamizole. The study drug was withdrawn after the 3rd episode, but the subject was followed until the end of the study (EOS) visit. However, the Appendix Table 2.7.4-22 (Figure 9) lists "withdrawal by patient" as the "(r)eason for study drug discontinuation" and the following for the "(r)eason in detail": "The detailed reason is unable to be confirmed.'

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In the AE narrative, the Applicant reported that the headaches had resolved. In the subject update provided by the Applicant after an Information Request, it was reported that the subject continued to experience severe headaches, which are still ongoing. There are times when the number of episodes can be as high as 5 per week. These episodes are unpredictable and tend to coincide with sudden increases in systolic blood pressure, requiring ad hoc use of sublingual captopril.

blocks.text: Clinical Reviewer's Comment: The subject received two medications during the TEAE of precordial chest pain, and the AE narrative stated that it was "not known" if therapeutic measures were administered. The Applicant's Summary of Clinical Safety reported that the subject's reason for study drug discontinuation was "withdrawal by patient," rather than the recurrent episodes of Grade 3 headache, and that the detailed reason "could not be confirmed, even though the reason was specified at the time of the study drug discontinuation. The AE narrative also stated that the headaches were resolved, even though the subject was followed up to 92 days after the study drug discontinuation (until EOS) and the update stated that these episodes had not resolved and had been frequently recurring.

blocks.text: Clinical Reviewer's Comment: Given that this subject experienced dyspepsia and was treated with FESTAL including ursodeoxycholic acid, commonly used to help digestion, especially of fatty meals, the abdominal pain experienced on the same day should not have been coded as "myalgia" PT (of abdomen). Of note, the combination product the subject received during TP2 for acute hepatitis is commonly used for treatment of fatty liver disease, liver cirrhosis, druginduced liver injury, and viral hepatitis. The review of his CRF, concomitant medications, and AE narratives suggests that this subject had TEAEs of dyspepsia, abdominal pain, and acute hepatitis that was unlikely from a viral origin. This subject's SAE of colon adenoma is further discussed in Serious Adverse Events.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Clinical Reviewer's Conclusion on the Quality and Integrity of the Safety Data: There are multiple instances of omission, inappropriate coding, and insufficient follow-up of TEAEs, as noted above. Also, description of the nature, status, or outcome of the TEAEs varied depending on the source of data provided by the Applicant. There may be more cases not captured by this review. Thus, the safety analyses shown here may not provide a reliable depiction of safety risks associated with CT-P43. Exhaustible examination of narratives, figures, and tables to cross-reference to determine consistency and validity for each data point for all TEAEs is not practicable. Therefore, lack of integrity in the study data compromises the assessment of clinical comparability on safety risk.

section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The phase 3 clinical study, Study CT-P43 3.1, provides the main comparative data for the safety review. During TP1, the overall rate of TEAEs was higher for the CT-P43 treatment group (37.1% - 155 events in 95 subjects), compared to the EU-Stelara treatment group (29.6% - 108 events in 75 subjects) (Table 20). The overall rates of SAEs were similar 1.6% (4 subjects) for the CT-P43 treatment and 1.6% (4 subjects) for the EU-Stelara treatment groups. No subjects discontinued treatment due to an AE during TP1.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: During TP2, TEAEs were reported in 34.0% (144 events in 86 subjects) for the CT-P43 maintenance, in 40.8% (78 events in 51 subjects) for the EU-Stelara maintenance and in 41.9% (95 events in 52 subjects) for the Switched to CT-P43 treatment groups. The overall rates of SAEs were similar in the CT-P43 maintenance, EU-Stelara maintenance (2.4%), and Switched to CT-P43 (1.6%) groups. However, slightly more subjects discontinued due to an AE in the CT- P43 maintenance group (2.0%) compared to the EU-Stelara maintenance (0.8%) and Switched to CT-P43 (TP2) (0.8%) groups (Table 36). The details for the discontinuations are discussed further in the section Dropouts and Discontinuations below.

blocks.text: Clinical Reviewer's Introductory Comments on Safety Analysis: In the safety analyses of the TEAEs for the main clinical comparability study, there were imbalances in hypertriglyceridemia, headaches/migraine, hypertension, Hepatobiliary SOC Disorders, Gastrointestinal ŠOC Disorders, and Neoplasm SOC Disorders with more cases reported in the CT-P43 treatment group, compared to the EU-Stelara treatment group. These TEAE imbalances were noted, despite similar Baseline characteristics, such as weight, BMl, age, sex, ethnicity (Table and Table), and prior use of immunosuppressants (Table). The subjects' medical history, in terms of cardiovascular disorders, hypertension, hepatobiliary disorders including steatohepatosis or steatohepatitis, hypertriglyceridemia, lipid disorders, and gastrointestinal disorders, and diabetes mellitus also showed similar rates of Baseline prevalence between CT-P43 and EUStelara treatment groups during TP1 and between CT-P43 maintenance and EU-Stelara maintenance treatment groups during TP2. (CT-P43 Post-hoc analysis - Study 3.1, Tables 1.12, 1.13, and 1.14, provided on March 14, 2024 by Celltrion, Inc.). The TEAE imbalances are discussed in more detail in the following sections: Serious Adverse Events, Treatment Emergent Adverse Events, and Adverse Events of Special Interest under Malignancies.

blocks.text: Acute pancreatitis: Subject was a 40-year-old white male. His medical history included plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, carpal tunnel syndrome, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, hyperuricemia, psoriatic arthropathy, spinal osteoarthritis, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. On Day 245, the participant experienced Grade 3 acute pancreatitis, which was considered a serious adverse event (SAE). Adverse events that occurred within a +/- 3-day window of the onset of the SAE included duodenitis (Grade 2), and hepatic steatosis (Grade 2). Concomitant medications taken at the onset of the SAE included: allopurinol, diclofenac sodium, insulin human injection, isophane, insulin lispro, lisinopril, and metformin hydrochloride. The investigator considered the AE to be unrelated to study medication. The event ended on Day 264 with a final outcome of recovered/resolved. Of note, at Screening and Baseline, his serum triglyceride level (TRIG) was reported at 11.44 mmol/L and 5.21 mmmol/L, respectively. His serum TRIG level increased (reached the limits of maximum detectable values of 50 mmmol/L on Day 80 and Day 85; 41.3 mmmol/L on Day 197) during the study before he experienced acute pancreatitis. His markedly increased serum triglyceride level from the Baseline was not documented as an AE. (b) (6)
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Also of note in this case, the reported imaging studies demonstrated findings consistent with chronic pancreatitis. Other testing that supports likely chronic changes in the pancreas is that the elevation in amylase was lower than expected for an acute episode (less than 3X the upper limit of normal). The narrative also states that the subject had historically used fibrates, commonly used to treat hypertriglyceridemia, and that the treatment was not well tolerated.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Clinical Reviewer's Assessment: This reviewer's determination on the causality of the acute pancreatitis is that it is likely related to the study drug. This determination is based on the fact that this SAE occurred in the setting of higher than the measurable limits of serum triglyceride levels that were markedly increased from his Baseline. Hypertriglyceridemia is a well-known cause of acute pancreatitis (Kiss et al. 2023). For this SAE, he was given treatment-emergent medications of ezetimibe, omega-3 fatty acids, and timonacic to treat hypertriglyceridemia, in addition to pantoprazole (no AE documented for pantoprazole). The subject may have had chronic pancreatitis prior to the study, but the worsening of his condition leading to an SAE of acute pancreatitis is likely due to CT-P43, given the imbalance of hypertriglyceridemia observed in the CT-P43 treatment group.

blocks.text: Colon adenoma: Subject (also discussed leading in 6.3 Review of Safety Data, Safety Analyses and Data Integrity) was a 41-year-old Asian male, and his medical history included plaque psoriasis. He had no prior history of systemic immunosuppressant use. On Day 1, he experienced "Grade 1 myalgia (abdomen)" and Grade 2 dyspepsia. The subject received FESTAL (ursodeoxycholic acid; cellulase ap; pancreatin; simethicone) for 3 days. The AEs were considered unrelated to the study medication and ended on Day 3 with a final outcome of recovered/resolved. On Day 233, a colon adenoma was reported, and it was considered an SAE and Grade 2 event. The lesion was found during a "pre-emptive health check-up" via endoscopy on Day 253, when the subject received cimetropium bromide, famotidine, ornithine aspartate, meperidine, flumazenil, midazolam, and propofol. The microscopic diagnosis from an endoscopic biopsy revealed a tubular adenoma. The investigator considered the AE to be unrelated to the study medication, and the event ended on Day 254 with a final outcome of recovered/resolved. On Day 302 the participant experienced acute hepatitis, a Grade 1 event. For the AE, the subject received GODEX (adenine hydrochloride; bifendate; carnitine orotate; cyanocobalamin; liver extract; pyridoxine hydrochloride; riboflavin). The investigator considered the AE to be unrelated to the study medication. Of note, the subject had increases in his serum triglyceride levels (as high as 6.29 mmol/L on Day 113) from his Screening (4.8 mmol/L) and Baseline (3.81 mmol/L) values during the study period. (b) (6)
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Clinical Reviewer's Assessment: The colon adenoma was classified as a Neoplasm SOC SAE and was said to be found during a "preemptive health check-up." However, given his age of 41 years, his GI symptoms of dyspepsia and "myalgia (abdonmen)" likely led to the subject's 2-day hospitalization, when exploratory endoscopy that may have included upper, as well as lower endoscopy was performed to determine the cause for his GI symptoms. (He, at a later timepoint during the study, also had acute hepatitis.) Therefore, the TEAE of colon adenoma could be an incidental finding during the endoscopy. However, in addition to the immunosuppressive effect of the drug class for ustekinumab, the clinical comparability study showed that the CT-P43 - treated group had worsening features of metabolic syndrome, such as hypertriglyceridemia, hyperglycemia, and hypertension. Since metabolic syndrome is associated with increased risk of cancers (Zhan et al. 2024; Hsu et al. 2022; Kitayama et al. 2009; Ahmed et al. 2006; Mazumder et al. 2023; Esposito et al. 2012; Siddiqqi et al. 2011), including formation of colon adenoma (Tabuchi et al. 2006) and its transition into colon cancer (Tabuchi et al. 2008), this reviewer's determination on the causality is that it is possibly related to the study drug.

blocks.text: Healthy Volunteers: In Study CT-P43 1.1, 86% of participants in CT-P43 group experienced at least 1 TEAE, compared to 82% in the US-Stelara group and 78% in the EU-Stelara group (Table 30). In Study CT-P43 1.2, 55% of participants in CT-P43 group experienced at least 1 TEAE, compared to 45% in the US-Stelara group and 50% in the EU-Stelara group (Table 58). While AEs were generally comparable across the treatment groups, it is notable that AEs related to the General Disorders and Àdministration Site Conditions SOC were more frequent in the CT-P43 group, compared to the US-Stelara and EU-Stelara groups. More specifically, in Study CT-P43 1.2, the repeat pharmacokinetic study that met the comparability criteria, injection site reactions were notably more common in the CT-P43-group (20%), compared to the US-Stelara (9%) and EU-Stelara (13%) groups. In Study CT-P43 1.1, in which the pharmacokinetic study failed, injection site reactions were reported in 12% in the CT-P43 group, compared to 9% in the USStelara group and 10% in the EÜ-Stelara group. The injection site reactions are discussed in more detail in Adverse Events of Special Interest under Injection Site Reactions. Otherwise, no particular pattern emerged from the rates of individual AEs across the treatment groups in the two single-dose PK studies with healthy volunteers (Table 57 and Table 58).

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Clinical Reviewer's Summary of TP1: During TP1, increased blood pressure or worsening of hypertension occurred predominantly in the CT-P43 group, and the risk difference was notable. All these subjects were started on long-term anti-hypertensives for this TEAE. Additionally, more cases of headache and dizziness were observed in the CT-P43 group, compared to the EUStelara group, and Grade 3 headaches occurred only in the CT-P43 group, and for one of the 2 subjects these severe headache episodes were later reported to coincide with marked increases in systolic blood pressure. For one of the 3 subjects with dizziness in the CT-P43 group, the onset coincided with worsening of hypertension, and it was later reported that the dizziness was significant and persistent. Taken together, worsening of hypertension, sometimes associated with concomitant headache or dizziness, seen in the CT-P43 group appears to be clinically meaningful.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The other notable risk difference was observed in the Metabolism and Nutrition Disorders SOC. Most TEAEs involved hyperlipidemia (hypertriglyceridemia, in particular) or hyperglycemia; AEs involving hyperglycemia were only observed in the CT-P43 group. The imbalances seen in the TEAEs with Gastrointestinal Disorders SOC (especially the ones involving upper GI inflammation) and Hepatobilliary Disorders SOC were notable, especially in that many of those subjects in the CT-P43 group had increases in the serum triglyceride levels from their Baseline during the study. Moreover, subjects with Gastrointestinal SOC TEAEs in the CT-P43 group only and not in the EU-Stelara group were started on proton pump inhibitors or medications often given for fatty liver disease during TP1.

blocks.text: Subjects with PSO (Study CT-P43 3.1) during TP2: The design of the second part of Study CTP43 3.1 allows for an assessment of safety that compares continuous treatment to that of switching products. Overall, 326 TEAEs were reported in 189 (37.6%) subjects (86 [34.0%], 51 [40.8%], and 52 [41.9%] subjects in the CT-P43 maintenance, Switched to CT-P43, and EUStelara maintenance groups, respectively) (Table 38). The majority of TEAEs during TP2 were mild or moderate in severity (Grade 1 or 2). The rates of Grade 3 or higher TEAEs were low, and the majority of them were singular events, but the highest incidence rate was observed in the switching arm, compared to the non-switching arms (Table 39). There were 23 Grade 3 events (10 [4.0%], 6 [4.8%], and 7 [5.6%] subjects in the CT-P43 maintenance, EU-Stelara maintenance, and Switched to CTP43 groups, respectively), 3 Grade 4 events (0 [0%], 1 [0.8%], and 2 [1.6%] subjects in the CT-P43 maintenance, EU-Stelara maintenance, and Switched to CT-P43 groups, respectively), and 1 Grade 5 (death) event in the CT-P43 maintenance group.

blocks.text: Strength of association - The incidence rate for the TEAE is higher in the CT-P43 group, compared to the EU-Stelara group (no subject in the EU-Stelara group reported this TEAE), and the incidence rate for the EU-Stelara group falls outside of the 95 th confidence interval of the incidence rate for the CT-P43 group, highlighting the notable risk difference.

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Temporality - All treatment-emergent adverse events meet this criterion with "effect" occurring after "cause."
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Biological gradient - This TEAE occurred in one subject during Treatment Period 1 (TP1), and more subjects reported the TEAE during Treatment Period 2 (TP2). The accumulated drug effect leading to more incidence in the CT-P43 treatment group during TP2 is consistent with the biological gradient criterion.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Plausibility & Analogy - Hypertriglyceridemia leading to adverse events such as steatohepatosis, acute pancreatitis, and gastroesophageal reflux symptoms have been welldocumented (see the Reference in the BMER). CT-P43 caused higher incidence rates of hypertriglyceridemia and its associated GI and hepatic adverse events, compared to EUStelara. Case reports of Stelara's association with hypertriglyceridemia and acute pancreatitis exist in literature; however, CT-P43, compared to EU-Stelara, seems to have a notably higher incidence in the clinical comparability trial.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Coherence - The imbalances seen with hypertriglyceridemia and its associated GI and hepatic TEAEs, and treatment-emergent medications for liver, dyslipidemia, and GI symptoms, including proton pump inhibitors, provide coherence in that all these events were seen at higher rates in the CT-P43 treated group, compared to the EU-Stelara group.

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Experimental evidence - The Applicant submitted a 4-week repeat-dose toxicity study that was conducted in Cynomolgus monkeys with CT-P43 and EU-Stelara. Subcutaneous doses of vehicle, 45 mg/kg CT-P43, and 45 mg/kg EU-Stelara were administered to Cynomolgus monkeys (3/sex/group) once weekly for 4 weeks (4 doses in total). There were no reported CTP43-specific findings from this study.

blocks.text: Clinical Reviewer's Summary of TP2: The imbalances were seen with hyperlipidemia, hyperglycemia, hepatic steatosis, and Gastrointestinal Disorders SOC, suggesting overall worsening of metabolic syndrome in the CT-P43 group, compared to the EU-Stelara group. Also, the imbalance seen in the number of neoplasms is concerning, because the definitive tissue diagnosis is lacking for the majority of these neoplasms. Features of metabolic syndrome, including hypertriglyceridemia, have been associated with the initiation and progression of various malignancies and precancerous neoplasms, including prostate cancer, breast cancer, cervical cancer, colon cancer, etc. (Mwangi et al. 2024; Tran et al. 2023; Zhang et al. 2021; Zhang et al. 2022; Raju et al. 2014; Vanhemelrijck et al. 2011; Dong et al. 2021; Wuermli et al. 2005; Arthur et al. 2016; Salgado-Montilla et al. 2015; Hernandez-Perez et al. 2022; GuerriosRivera et al. 2023; Liu et al. 2023; Esposito et al. 2012; Russo et al. 2008; Agresti et al. 2016; Rosato et al. 2011; Lebdai et al. 2018; Tabuchi et al. 2008; Tabuchi et al. 2006; Hsu et al. 2022; Ahmet et al. 2006; Siddiqui et al. 2011; Kitayama et al. 2009; Wan et al. 2022; Zhan et al. 2024; Mazumder et al. 2023; Wu et al. 2022; Sun et al. 2020). It is notable that there were 2 cases of goiter in the CT-P43 group, compared to none in the EU-Stelara group. Hypertriglyceridemia and other features of metabolic syndrome have been associated with thyroid nodules in several studies (Tran et al. 2023; Zhang et al. 2021; Zhang et al. 2022); in one of these studies prevalence of thyroid nodules with ultrasound features suspicious for malignancy were as high as 36.9% (Tran et al. 2023 ) .

blocks.text: The prescribing information for US-Stelara carries the following warnings and precautions: infections (including cellulitis, pneumonia, sepsis, zoster, abscess, and tuberculosis), malignancies, hypersensitivity reactions, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), and noninfectious pneumonia.

blocks.text: The Applicant identified the following AEs as Events of Interest: serious systemic hypersensitivity reactions, facial palsy, pustular or erythrodermic psoriasis, serious infection (including mycobacterial and salmonella infections), malignancy, cardiovascular events, reversible posterior leukoencephalopathy syndrome (RPLS), serious depression including suicidality, and venous thromboembolism.

blocks.text: Overall, the proportion of subjects experiencing AESIs were similar across all arms for the entire duration of the study (before and after re-randomization), with the exception of more COVID-19 infections in the EU-Stelara/ABP 654 arm in TP02 than the arms that continued on the same drug as in TP01.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: As shown in Table 22, all treatment groups in Study CT-P43 3.1 showed similar rates of Infection, overall. During TP1 of Study CT-P43 3.1, infections and infestations were reported at a rate of 14.5%; the CT-P43 treatment group had 15.2%, and the EU-Stelara group had 11.9%. COVID-19, followed by upper respiratory infection, was the most common dictionary-derived term cause. During TP2 of Study CT-P43, infections and infestations were reported at a rate of 18.7%; the CT-P43 treatment group had 18.3%, and EU-Stelara group had 20.8%. During TP2, COVID-19 (6.1%), upper respiratory infection (4.1%), and latent tuberculosis (2.9%) were the most common dictionary-derived term causes for Infections and infestations SOC.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Infections that were considered serious were rare during Study CT-P43 3.1, with comparable rates of serious infection across the treatment groups. COVID-19 pneumonia was the most common serious infection reported, at a rate of 0.8% in the study.

blocks.text: Overall, the AEs related to injection site reactions were more common with CT-P43 administration. In Study CT-P43 1.2 the rate of injection site reactions was 20% in the CT-P43 group, compared to 9% in the US-Stelara and 13% in the EU-Stelara groups (Table 31). In Study CT-P43 1.1 the rate of injection site reactions was slightly higher in the CT-P43 group (11.7 %), compared to the US-Stelara group (9.0%) and the EU-Stelara group (10.2%) (Table 30). The increased rates with CT-P43 repeated in Study CT-P43 3.1, albeit at low rates (Table 22). During TP1, the CT-P43 group had 1.2%, compared to 0.8% in the EU-Stelara group; during TP2, the CT-P43 group had 0.8%, compared to 0% in the EU-Stelara group.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Clinical Reviewer's Conclusion on Safety during the Clinical Comparability Study: The safety review found instances of improper coding, omissions, and insufficient follow-up of the TEAEs during the clinical comparability study, CT-P43 3.1. Lack of confidence in the quality and integrity of the safety data compromises the process of determining whether or not there is a clinically meaningful difference in terms of safety risk between CT-P43 and EU-Stelara. Furthermore, there were imbalances observed in multiple PT and SOC TEAE categories with higher numbers of incidence for the CT-P43 group, compared to the EU-Stelara group. There was a higher incidence rate of worsening hypertension in the CT-P43 group during TP1 that led to long-term antihypertensive medications. Some of these subjects experienced severe or persistent headaches or dizziness. Two subjects discontinued the study drug, due to persistent Grade 3 headaches. There were also higher incidences of hypertriglyceridemia and hyperglycemia in the CT-P43 group, and many of these subjects experienced Gastrointestinal Disorders SOC AEs and/or Hepatobiliary Disorders SOC AEs. Neoplasm SOC was another area of imbalance with one confirmed malignancy and three or more undefined neoplasms suspicious for possible malignancy, all occurring in the CT-P43 group. Although the deceased subject in the CT-P43 group had known risk factors for cardiovascular disease, the death from fatal myocardial infarction may be possibly related to CT-P43, given the worsening of features of metabolic syndrome observed in the CT-P43 group. Finally, severe TEAEs, SAEs, and death leading to study drug discontinuation were noted only in the CT-P43 treatment group, not in the EU-Stelara treatment group.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In summary, in addition to the concerns regarding the data quality, there are safety risk imbalances observed during the clinical comparability study. CT-P43 demonstrated potentially significant increase in safety risk with worsening of features of metabolic syndrome and its associated conditions, compared to EU-Stelara (and thus US-licensed Stelara). Because worsening of metabolic syndrome, which is known to be prevalent in psoriasis patients, will be more difficult to attribute to its source of causation in a post-marketing setting, CT-P43 could effect negative health outcomes for patients for a long time without ever being withdrawn from marketing. Moreover, there are two other ustekinumab biosimilars that have already been approved, and CT-P43 will not add to the current treatment landscape of the diseases for which the Applicant is seeking indication. Therefore, this reviewer recommends, in the strongest term possible, against approval of CT-P43. CT-P43 has the potential to have a significant negative impact, without additional benefit, on public health.

blocks.text: The primary clinical reviewer has identified two areas of concern for her recommendation of a non-approvable action. This reviewer met with the primary clinical reviewer on several occasions to understand her position and assessment of the data and I have considered her assessment in detail. I do not believe that either issue rises to the level of rendering this application non-approvable. The first concern that the primary clinical reviewer has identified is that certain minor inconsistencies in the collection and reporting of data imply that there are significant data quality issues that do not support approvability. Second, the primary clinical reviewer notes that certain imbalances in the PT and TEAE data in the comparative clinical study provide sufficient evidence to conclude that there are clinically meaningful differences between CT-P43 and US-licensed Stelara. The primary reviewer's conclusions about data integrity and CT-P43 are not supported by the data. While it is not feasible for this reviewer to address all instances in which I believe the clinical reviewer's methodology and/or conclusions were unsound, in my review below, I will address the main concerns identified by the primary clinical reviewer in Sections 6.3.1, 6.3.2, and 6.3.3.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: On the first issue, in Section 6.3.1., the primary reviewer notes "There are multiple instances of omission, inappropriate coding, and insufficient follow-up of TEAEs, as noted above. Also, description of the nature, status, or outcome of the TEAEs varied depending on the source of data provided by the Applicant. There may be more cases not captured by this review. Thus, the safety analyses shown here may not provide a reliable depiction of safety risks associated with CT-P43."
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: This reviewer does not concur that the inconsistencies identified by the primary reviewer indicate a significant issue with data integrity. Clinical trials involve managing large volumes of data from multiple sources. This can be challenging due to human error, inconsistent data capture or subjects lost to follow-up. It is common to have minor but inconsequential inconsistencies or omissions in medical history collection, safety-event follow-up, or adverse event coding. The inconsistencies identified by the primary reviewer fall squarely in this category. Moreover, clinical inspections were conducted to assess the adequacy of data generated in the Study CT-P43 3.1. Thirty-four study centers in four countries (Estonia, Korea, Poland, and Ukraine) screened 574 subjects and enrolled 509 subjects. Of these study sites, the Office of Scientific Investigation (OSI) conducted site inspections at two select sites. The two clinical investigators selected for inspections (Drs. Jaworski and Daniluk) were selected based on size of enrollment at their study sites. OSI reviewed records of 85 subjects from both sites combined. The inspections did not find significant concerns regarding the oversight of the clinical study or GCP or regulatory compliance. There were no discrepancies in the submitted data when compared to the source data. No unusual enrollment practice or patterns were identified. OSI concluded that, based on the results of these inspections, data generated by the inspected clinical investigators were acceptable in support of the proposed application. Refer to the OSI inspection summary dated January 18, 2024.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The primary reviewer's expectation that scrutiny of all study sites is necessary for assurance in data quality is impractical and not in line with the Agency's standard practice. The most impactful sites in this study were sampled. This sampling along with a specified protocol and the applicant's internal monitoring measures is a reasonable approach to ensure data quality across study sites. Claiming that there is a data integrity issue due to not all sites being inspected, would be holding this applicant to a different standard. The number of records included in the inspection is a reasonable representation of the data and is sufficient to understand whether there were significant data integrity issues that would impact the Agency's assessment.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In Section 6.3.1, the primary clinical reviewer notes a single case of an inaccurate characterization of a subject discontinuation e.g., reported as "withdrawal by subject" instead of "due to adverse event" . This characterization does not impact the safety analysis. Total discontinuations were provided, occurred infrequently, and were similar across treatment arms. During Treatment Period I, a total of 7 subjects (1.4%) discontinued the study drug and terminated from the study prior to Week 16. The proportion of subjects with treatment or study discontinuation before Week 16 was similar between the CT-P43 group and EU-Stelara group. After re-randomization at Week 16, among the 502 subjects, 15 (3.0%) subjects discontinued the study drug (10 (4.0%), 3 (2.4%), and 2 (1.6%) in the CT-P43 maintenance, EU-Stelara maintenance, and switched to CT-P43 groups, respectively).
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Therefore, the data and information in the application do not suggest any data quality issues that would preclude approval. Further, the single discontinuation case discussed above does not compromise the FDA's ability to assess for whether clinically meaningful differences in safety exist between CT-P43 and US-Stelara. There is sufficient data and information in this application to conclude that the provided clinical data can be relied upon to support a demonstration that there are no clinically meaningful differences between CT-P43 and US-Stelara.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: On the second issue, which the primary clinical reviewer seems to have considered as independent from the data quality issue discussed above, is a conclusion that that there are clinical differences between CT-P43 and US-Stelara based on observed imbalances in the safety data from the comparative clinical study (CCS). Interpetation of comparisons beyond Week 16 are limited due to the crossover of EU-Stelara treated subjects to CT-P43 at Week 16 in Study CT-P43 3.1. This results in a higher number of patients who received 5 doses (up to Week 40) of study drug in the CT-P43 group as compared to the EU-Stelara group (243 patients and 121 patients, respectively). Furthermore, in this case, it is not appropriate to base such a conclusion of clinically meaningful differences solely on the CCS because the study lacks the sensitivity and is underpowered to demonstrate meaningful differences in individual adverse events. Rather, the totality of evidence submitted to support the application is proper and supports a demonstration that there are no clinically meaningful differences between CT-P43 and US-Stelara in terms of safety, purity, and potency. A summary of the evidence supporting this conclusion is described below:

blocks.text: The comparative efficacy of CT-P43 and EU-Stelara was evaluated in Study CTP43 3.1, a double-blind, randomized, multi-center, parallel-group, efficacy and safety study in subjects with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (PsO) during 40 weeks of treatment. Comparative efficacy was assessed for the primary endpoint, the mean percent improvement in PASI at Week 12. The 90% confidence interval (CI) for the treatment difference based on the mean percent change from baseline in PASI at Week 12 for the Modified Intent-to-Treat (mITT) Analysis Set, the supportive per- protocol (PP) Analysis Set, as well as sensitivity analyses, all fall within the similarity margins of ±10 [MITT: (-0.23, 4.32), PP: (- 0.29, 4.29)]. Thus, the study demonstrated no meaningful differences between the CT-P43 and EU-Stelara as assessed by the primary efficacy endpoint. In addition, secondary efficacy endpoints, when considered with the primary endpoint results, also support a demonstration that there are no clinical meaningful differences between the CT-P43 and US-Stelara.

blocks.text: Even looking at the CCS in isolation, the frequency of TEAEs, SAEs and discontinuations were generally comparable between the CT-P43 and EU-Stelara groups in the clinical study. Overall, serious adverse events were infrequent, and a single death occurred during the study. In Section 6.3.2, in reference to the single death, the primary clinical reviewer states "Although the subject had risk factors for myocardial infarction, such as obesity and smoking…[the] causality of death is that it's possibly related to the study drug. This is based on the overall safety data imbalance with disproportionate worsening of cardiovascular risk factors, such as hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, and hyperglycemia, observed in the CT-P43 treatment group". The reviewer's conclusion is inappropriate because there is insufficient evidence to causally link the death from myocardial infarction to CT-P43 or to worsening of risk factors brought on by CT-P43 treatment. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is one of the major comorbidities in patients with psoriatic disease. In addition to having psoriasis, an independent risk factor for CVD, this subject also carried additional risk factors (obesisty and tobacco use) confounding the attribution of causality. Another potentially confounding factor could be the contemporenous administration of a vaccine which has been associated with cardiovascular adverse events for men of a similar age 11 . This reviewer finds that the investigator's conclusion that this death is unrelated to treatment with CT-P43 is reasonable. Furthermore, a single reported death is not sufficient to conclude that CT-P43 poses a different CVD risk than US-Stelara.

blocks.text: For concerns raised by the primary reviewer, information requests were sent were sent to the applicant requesting additional details and analyses on various adverse events and laboratory values.
