blocks.label: text
blocks.text: This reviewer does not agree with the primary reviewer's analysis of the data. For example, imbalances observed by comparing system organ class (SOC) groupings are not appropriate because SOC groupings contain AEs that are only related by the involved organ but are often unrelated by pathology and etiology; for example abdominal hernia and constipation are both under the SOC of gastrointestinal disorders but are not clinically related. Adverse events were inappropriately lumped in order to demonstrate an imbalance. This reviewer also finds limitations with the primary reviewer's assessment of causality in a number of AE cases. For many of the subjects whose TEAE is assessed by the primary reviewer as related to CT-P43, there are multiple confounders and there is a high possibility that the TEAE is related to a flare or progression of an already existing condition.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: For example, the primary clinical reviewer notes in Section 6.3.2 that "the causality of the acute pancreatitis is that it is likely related to the study drug. This determination is based on the fact that this SAE occurred in the setting of higher than the measurable limits of serum triglyceride levels that were markedly increased from his Baseline …The subject may have had chronic pancreatitis prior to the study, but the worsening of his condition leading to an SAE of acute pancreatitis is likely due to CT-P43, given the imbalance of hypertriglyceridemia observed in the CT-P43 treatment group." It is inappropriate to make conclusions about the potential causal relationship between the study drug and acute pancreatitis based on one subject, especially in the context of a patient with findings suggestive of a history of chronic pancreatitis. Chronic pancreatitis is characterized by a progressive fibro-inflammatory process and this acute flare is more likely to be related to a pre-existing condition.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The complexity of the cross-over study design should also be considered in the interpretation. This design is intended to provide a substantive descriptive assessment of whether a single transition would result in a major risk in terms of hypersensitivity, immunogenicity, or other reactions. It is not appropriate to attribute individual events to CT-P43 in subjects who have switched from treatment with EU-Stelara to CT-P43, or to consider individual events outside of the context of the switching arm as a whole. Furthermore, attribution of causality for expected long latency events, like malignancy, that occur after limited exposure are biologically implausible or unreasonable to associate the AEs with the study drug.

blocks.text: The Applicant has developed CT-P43 as a proposed interchangeable biosimilar to USStelara and is seeking licensure of CT-P43 for the same indications, same dosage form, strengths and routes of administration as US-Stelara.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Applicant provided sufficient justification that CT-P43 can be expected to produce the same clinical result as US-licensed Stelara in any given patient. The scientific justification considered the factors that are described in the FDA guidance for industry, Considerations in Demonstrating Interchangeability with a Reference Product (refer also to Section 6.6 Extrapolation).

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Applicant also provided sufficient scientific justification that the risk in terms of safety or diminished efficacy of alternating or switching between use of CT-P43 and USlicensed Stelara is not greater than the risk of using US-licensed Stelara without such alteration or switch. The Applicant referenced the comparative analytical data provided in their application that evaluated and compared critical quality attributes of CT-P43 and US-Stelara and the results from the comparative clinical study (Study CT-P43 3.1) to support their justification. The Applicant also described that the results from the single transition included in Study CT-P43 3.1 provided supportive evidence of a low immunogenic risk and no safety concerns with switching between CT-P43 and USStelara.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In addition to the plaque psoriasis indication, the Applicant is seeking licensure of CTP43 (ustekinumab-stba) for the following indication under the purview of DRTM:
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Treatment of patients 6 years or older with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA)
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In their application, the Applicant has provided justification for extrapolation of data and relevant supportive information for licensure of CT-P43 as an interchangeable biosimilar for the above indication for which licensure is sought and for which US-Stelara has been previously licensed and CT-P43 has not been directly studied.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: First, as summarized above, the Applicant submitted data and information to demonstrate that CT-P43 is highly similar to US-Stelara and that there are no clinically meaningful differences between CT-P43 and US-Stelara in terms of safety, purity, and potency based on similar clinical pharmacokinetics (PK) (study CT-P43 1.2), and similar efficacy, safety, and immunogenicity in patients with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (PsO) (study CT-P43 3.1).
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Further, the additional points considered in the scientific justification for extrapolation of data and information to support licensure of CT-P43 for the treatment of PsA are described below.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Mechanism of Action (MOA)
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: CT-P43 is a recombinant humanized monoclonal immunoglobulin G (IgG) 1kappa antibody that binds to the p40 protein subunit used by both interleukin (IL)-12 and IL-23 cytokines. As these cytokines are involved in inflammatory responses, binding to p40 prevents downstream IL-12 and IL-23 activity and, thereby, attenuates an immune response.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In comprehensive in vitro comparative testing, CT-P43 has been shown to be functionally similar to ustekinumab. These data demonstrate that the biologic activity and potency of CT-P43 have a high degree of similarity to ustekinumab and provide additional evidence that the MOA of the two products, binding to the p40 subunit of the IL-23 and IL-12 and, subsequently, preventing the interaction of IL-23 and IL-12 with IL12Rb1, is the same.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Applicant adequately addressed each of the known and potential mechanisms of action of Stelara and submitted data to support the conclusion that CT-P43 and USStelara have the same mechanisms for the sought indication of PsA to the extent that the mechanisms of action are known or can reasonably be determined.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Pharmacokinetics (PK)
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The clinical development program to support similarity of CT-P43 to US-Stelara includes a PK study in healthy male subjects and one comparative clinical study in subjects with moderate to severe PsO. Similar PK was demonstrated between CT-P43, EU-Stelara, and US-Stelara in study CT-P43 1.2, a randomized, double-blind, parallel group, 3-arm PK similarity study in healthy Japanese males. This study is reviewed in the section on Clinical Pharmacology. Importantly, CT-P43 was demonstrated to be highly similar to US-Stelara, as discussed in the section on CMC/Product Quality; therefore, there are no product-related attributes that would increase the uncertainty that the PK/biodistribution may differ between CT-P43 and US-Stelara in the rheumatology indication for licensure (PsA). Thus, a similar PK profile would be expected between CT-P43 and US-Stelara in patients with PsA.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)

blocks.text: Immunogenicity
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Immunogenicity of CT-P43 was examined in the PK similarity study CT-P43 1.2, healthy male subjects) and comparative clinical study (CT-P43 3.1, subjects with PsO), and development of binding and neutralizing ADAs was numerically lower or similar for the CT-P43 treatment groups compared with US-Stelara and EU-Stelara. As reviewed elsewhere in this document, the clinical PK and safety data support that the observed differences are not clinically meaningful. The Agency has concluded that there are sufficient data to support similar immunogenicity between CT-P43 and US-Stelara with repeat dosing in subjects with PsO and after a single dose in healthy subjects. Accordingly, similar immunogenicity would be expected between CT-P43 and USStelara in patients with PsA. In addition, DRTM notes that similar rates of antibodies to US-Stelara were seen in clinical studies of subjects with PsO and PsA. [1]
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations

blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Applicant provided adequate justification that similar or decreased immunogenicity is expected between CT-P43 and US-Stelara for PsA.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Toxicity
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
6.6.1. DIVISION of RHEUMATOLOGY and TRANSPLANT MEDICINE (DRTM)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Applicant demonstrated that there are no meaningful differences in safety between CT-P43 and EU-Stelara in subjects with PsO and between CT-P43, EU-Stelara, and US-Stelara following single doses in healthy subjects. Additionally, in controlled clinical studies of US-Stelara submitted to support its approval, as described in the approved labeling, 12 the types of adverse events and their rates were similar across indications. Coupled with the demonstration of analytical and PK similarity between CT-P43, USStelara, and EU-Stelara, a similar safety profile would be expected between CT-P43 and US-Stelara in patients with PsA.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Executive Summary: Consistent with the principles of the FDA guidance for industry Scientific Considerations in Demonstrating Biosimilarity to a Reference Product (April 2015), 13 the Division of Gastroenterology (DG) concludes that the Applicant has provided sufficient scientific justification to support extrapolation of data submitted in the application to support licensure of CT-P43 as an interchangeable biosimilar to US licensed Stelara, under section 351(k) of the PHS Act, for the non-studied indications of Crohn's disease (CD), and ulcerative colitis (UC) in adults. The scientific justification based on the mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics (PK), immunogenicity, and safety supporting this conclusion are summarized in the following paragraphs.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Mechanism of Action: The mechanisms of action of ustekinumab that are relevant to moderate to severe active plaque psoriasis (PsO; the studied clinical study population) are also relevant to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) (i.e., CD and UC). The Applicant provided data to support that CT-P43 has the same known and potential mechanisms of action as US-Stelara, which supports extrapolation to indications not directly studied in the CT-P43 clinical program. Ustekinumab belongs to the pharmacologic class of interleukin (IL)-23 and IL-12 antagonists. It is a human IgG1қ monoclonal antibody that binds with specificity to the p40 protein subunit used by both the IL-12 and IL-23 cytokines that are involved in inflammatory and immune responses, such as natural killer cell activation and CD4+ T-cell differentiation and activation. In the in vitro models, ustekinumab was shown to disrupt IL-12 and IL-23 mediated signaling and cytokine cascades by disrupting the interaction of these cytokines with a shared cell-surface receptor chain, IL-12Rβ1. The cytokines IL-12 and IL-23 have been implicated as important contributors to the chronic inflammation that is a hallmark of CD and UC. 14 The biological activities of CT-P43 and US-Stelara were evaluated by a comprehensive set of comparative functional and binding assays. The product quality reviewers concluded the acceptability of the comparative analytical assessments. Biological activities relevant to the primary mode of action i.e., IL-12 and IL-23 receptor binding and inhibition assays, as well as those related to IFN-γ secretion inhibition and IL-12/IL-23 inhibition reporter assays were similar across CT-P43 vs. US- Stelara. Overall, these data support the determination that CT-P43 and US-Stelara are highly similar. Data support the conclusion that CT-P43 and US-Stelara utilize the same mechanism(s) of action, to the extent such mechanism(s) are known.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Pharmacokinetics (PK): Study CT-P43 1.2., was a randomized, double-blind, parallel group, single dose, PK similarity study conducted in healthy Japanese adult male subjects. The clinical pharmacology reviewers concluded that the data from this study support a demonstration of PK similarity between CT-P43 vs. US-Stelara, CT-P43 vs. EU-Stelara, and US-Stelara vs. EU-Stelara in healthy subjects (refer to Section 5 Clinical Pharmacology Evaluation and Recommendations). Available data on USStelara do not indicate any major differences in PK based on disease state. It is reasonable to conclude that PK for CT-P43 is expected to be similar between patients with PsO (the studied population) and those with IBD.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Immunogenicity: In the CT-P43 development program, immunogenicity was evaluated in populations that were considered sensitive for detecting meaningful differences (healthy subjects and PsO). While some differences were noted in the ADA incidence across the treatment groups in both study populations, per the Clinical Pharmacology reviewers, the impact of immunogenicity on PK, efficacy, and/or safety between CT-P43 and US-/EU-Stelara was generally comparable and not considered to be clinically meaningful. Additionally, there were no meaningful differences in the rates of ADA in those subjects that underwent a single transition from EU-Stelara to CT-43 in Study CT-P43 3.1., compared to those that remained on EU-Stelara. Therefore, it is reasonable to conclude that the impact of immunogenicity in patients with IBD receiving CT-P43 would be similar to that observed in patients with PsO receiving US-Stelara. Refer to Section 5 Clinical Pharmacology Evaluation and Recommendations of this review for further details.
section_path: 6. Statistical and Clinical Evaluation and Recommendations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Safety: The safety of CT-P43 compared to EU-Stelara was assessed in the comparative clinical study CT-P43 3.1. conducted in patients with PsO, and supported by a single dose, PK similarity study CT-P43 1.2. conducted in healthy subjects. Safety assessments in the two clinical studies included adverse events (AEs), physical examinations, vital signs, clinical laboratory testing, and immunogenicity assessments. The frequency of TEAEs, SAEs and discontinuations due to AEs were generally comparable between the CT-P43 and EU-Stelara groups in the clinical study. In addition, as previously noted, a single transition from EU-Stelara to CT-P43 was assessed as part of the study. No meaningful differences in the incidence of adverse events, were observed in patients with PsO that underwent a single transition, compared to those that remained on their randomized treatment (CT-P43 or EUStelara). Refer to the Section 6.3. Review of Safety Data, for further details. In controlled clinical studies of US-licensed Stelara, as described in the approved labeling, the types of adverse events and their rates were similar across indications. The safety profile of CT-P43 has been shown to be similar to that of EU-Stelara in patients with PsO. When combined with the adequate PK bridging between US-Stelara and EUStelara from the healthy subject study CT-P43 1.2., as well as similar product quality attributes, PK, and immunogenicity, the safety profile in the IBD population is expected to be generally comparable to that observed in patients with PsO, and overall, the data support extrapolation to the non-studied IBD population.

blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.text: Under the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) (section 505B of the FD&C Act), all applications for new active ingredients, new indications, new dosage forms, new dosing regimens, or new routes of administration are required to contain a pediatric assessment to support dosing, safety, and effectiveness of the product for the claimed indication unless this requirement is waived, deferred, or inapplicable. Section 505B(l) of the FD&C Act provides that a biosimilar product that has not been determined to be interchangeable with the reference product is considered to have a "new active ingredient" for purposes of PREA, and a pediatric assessment is generally required. However, since this application will receive a complete response, issuance of a PMR is not applicable.

blocks.text: The container closure integrity test (CCIT) dye ingress method used for stability testing of CT-P43 IV drug product vials is not validated to ensure reproducibility of results between different analysts. blocks.label: text
blocks.text: I concur with the recommendation by the Office of Pharmaceutical Quality (OPQ) that the data submitted in this application are not sufficient to support the conclusion that the manufacture of CT-P43 is well-controlled and leads to a product that is pure, safe, and potent. OPQ review of submitted data identified multiple product quality deficiencies including inadequate qualification of reference standards, inadequate control of drug product, and insufficient data to support sterility assurance of the CT-P43 130 mg/26 mL single-dose vial drug product. OPQ is not recommending an approval of this BLA until the product quality deficiencies are satisfactorily resolved.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Therefore, this BLA application will be issued a complete response (CR) based on identified product quality deficiencies. Specific deficiencies and what would be required to resolve them will be listed in CR letter.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: I concur with the CDTL's recommendation that the submitted clinical data is sufficient to conclude that the investigational product CT-P43 can be approved as an interchangeable biosimilar product.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: I do not concur with the primary clinical reviewer's opinion that there are clinically meaningful differences between CT-P43 and the reference product due to safety concerns.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The CDTL portion of this review elaborates in detail on the key issues raised by the primary clinical reviewer and I agree with the CDTL's assessment. To discuss the analysis and interpretation of the data submitted, the review team had several internal meetings with the clinical reviewer. After open discussion about the data, the team was unable to reach alignment with the clinical reviewer. I have carefully considered her analysis and views along with the analysis and views of other members of the review team in reaching the conclusion that the clinical data are sufficient to support approval of CT-P43 as an interchangeable biosimilar product.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The potential issue with data integrity raised by the primary reviewer is not supported by the OSI Division after they conducted an inspection of 2 sites with the largest study enrollment.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The primary reviewer's concern about an imbalance in certain adverse events does not suggest that there are clinically meaningful differences between CT-P43 and USStelara. As the CDTL review explains, the study conducted by the applicant is not sufficiently powered for safety and the imbalance in adverse events such as headaches, elevated blood pressures, etc. does not raise safety concerns that would preclude approval. These adverse events that are identified by the primary reviewer, by regulatory definition of severity, are not severe, do not appear in clusters, and do not suggest that there is a clinically meaningful difference between CT-P43 and US-Stelara. Imbalances such as those indicated in the clinical review are common and could, in part, be explained by the greater number of subjects who received CT-P43 vs EUStelara in the comparative clinical study.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In conclusion, the data and information submitted by the Applicant, including adequate justification for extrapolation of data and information, demonstrate that CT-P43 can be approved as an interchangeable biosimilar product, once the deficiencies described in the Complete Response letter are addressed.

blocks.text: A 4-week repeat-dose toxicity study was conducted in Cynomolgus monkeys with CTP43 and EU-Stelara (Study# 8416958, GLP). blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Following study CT-P43 1.1, the applicant investigated the root cause for failure in PK similarity demonstration. It was determined that generally, there was greater protein content in the clinical batches of CT-P43 which were used in the Study CT-P43 1.1 compared to the protein content values of EU-Stelara and US-Stelara batches. Following Table 37 shows a comparison among the three products with regards to protein content. It shows that CT-P43 batch 0NGA05 had closer value of protein content when compared with the US-Stelara and EU stelara while the other CT-P43 batches had notably larger protein content values than those of EU-Stelara and US-Stelara batches.

blocks.text: When the serum concentration of study drug and PK parameters were analyzed by batch, it was found that subjects who were treated with CT-P43 batch 0NGA05, the difference between CT-P43, US-Stelara and EU-Stelara was smaller with regards to AUC and Cmax.
